15714               	;
15715               	; 	' A SOUND STILL PLAYING WHEN THE ROUND ENDS IS ALLOWED TO FINISH.
15716               	; 	'
15717               	; 	' This used to open with a bare `GOSUB snd_off`, which cut it dead. That
15718               	; 	' was not an accident: the decay counters are ticked by the MAIN LOOP, and
15719               	; 	' this pause REPLACES the main loop, so a tone left latched with nothing
15720               	; 	' ticking it hangs for the full ninety frames -- the sticky-audio failure
15721               	; 	' this game has already shipped twice. The answer is to DRAIN the counters
15722               	; 	' rather than to stop silencing.
15723               	; 	'
15724               	; 	' CLEAR THE PENDING LATCHES FIRST. sf* flags are sounds that have not
15725               	; 	' happened yet; left set, the drain below would START one and the pause
15726               	; 	' would end with a fresh note ringing into the next round.
15727               	; 	'
15728               	; 	' THEN TICK sfx_tick WHOLE, not some decay-only part of it. The five
15729               	; 	' counters do not all live in one place: sot, sht and spt are a block at
15730               	; 	' the tail, but spz (the prize arpeggio) and swt (the jump warble) tick up
15731               	; 	' among the code that starts sounds. Draining only the tail would finish a
15732               	; 	' footstep and still cut the arpeggio, which is the one effect with a
15733               	; 	' phrase worth saving. Calling the whole routine also leaves the write
15734               	; 	' order on CHANNEL 2 alone, which spz and spt share.
15735               	; 	'
15736               	; 	' EVERY THIRD FRAME, because the main loop runs about 2.5 frames per pass
15737               	; 	' and this loop waits one frame per turn. Ticking every frame would play
15738               	; 	' everything at two and a half times its tuned speed. Three frames a tick
15739               	; 	' is ~17% slow and gives 30 ticks against the longest effect's 20 passes.
15740               	; 	'
15741               	; 	' THE LOOP COUNTS TICKS, NOT FRAMES, which is what makes the pacing free.
15742               	; 	' Counting 91 frames and firing on every third needs a second counter, an
15743               	; 	' increment and a test -- 48 bytes, on a fixed area with 66 left. Counting
15744               	; 	' 31 TICKS of three WAITs each is the same 93 frames and the same three
15745               	; 	' frames per tick, with none of that. The duration changes by two frames.
15746               	; 	'
15747               	; 	' snd_off still runs at the END, as the backstop for anything the drain
15748               	; 	' did not finish.
15749               	; pause_beat:
15750               cvb_PAUSE_BEAT

15799               	; 	' `SOUND ch,f,0` the last tone sustains for ever. And the second argument

16177               	; 	' it was the wrong instrument for the job: the last ten seconds are the
16178               	; 	' busiest part of a round, so a repeating tone arrives exactly when the
16179               	; 	' player most needs to hear the hazards, and it fought the prize arpeggio
16180               	; 	' for channel 2 as well. The flash says the same thing and says it in the
16181               	; 	' place the player is already looking.
16182               	;
16183               	; 	' FOOTSTEPS ARE NOISE, AND ON THE NOISE CHANNEL -- testsounds variant A.
16184               	; 	'
16185               	; 	' They were two alternating TONES on channel 0, which is neither what the
16186               	; 	' original does nor a good use of a channel: the recording says a footstep
16187               	; 	' is a short burst of white noise, and channel 3 was sitting unused while
16188               	; 	' the footsteps and the jump sweep shared channel 0 and had to take turns.
16189               	; 	'
16190               	; 	' TESTSOUNDS RUN D: a SHORT tick at the measured RATE.
16191               	; 	'
16192               	; 	' The two dials are independent and both were tried at the bench. The
16193               	; 	' 2600 plays a 64 ms burst every 165 ms -- six a second -- and variant A
16194               	; 	' copies both. Ten a second was tried on the way here and reads as
16195               	; 	' hurrying rather than running. What D changes is not the cadence but the
16196               	; 	' TICK: two frames rather than four, and a notch louder to carry at half
16197               	; 	' the length. Same six a second, less of it.
16198               	; 	'
16199               	; 	' EIGHT A SECOND, AND THE ACCUMULATOR NOW CARRIES ITS REMAINDER.
16200               	; 	'
16201               	; 	' sfw counted pixels and the trigger did `sfw = 0`, THROWING AWAY whatever
16202               	; 	' was past the threshold. kspd is about four pixels a pass, so a threshold
16203               	; 	' of 17 did not fire at 17 -- it fired at the first multiple past it, about
16204               	; 	' 20, and every rate this was ever set to came out slower than the number
16205               	; 	' said: the "six a second" was 5.2 and the "ten" that read as hurrying was
16206               	; 	' really 8.7. Subtracting the threshold instead keeps the fraction, so the
16207               	; 	' rate is what it claims to be at any walking speed.
16208               	; 	'
16209               	; 	' MEASURED OFF THE COLECOVISION: 14 px, about 7.4 a second.
16210               	; 	'
16211               	; 	' It was 15 px and 6.9 a second, picked between an 8.0 that read as
16212               	; 	' slightly hurried and a 6.1 that read as trudging -- a judgement between
16213               	; 	' two other judgements, with nothing underneath it. The ColecoVision
16214               	; 	' recording settles it: footfalls land every 0.130 s across a twelve-second
16215               	; 	' continuous run, which is 7.7 a second, and that is the one finding in the
16216               	; 	' whole sound analysis the method resolves EXACTLY -- a rhythm rather than a
16217               	; 	' pitch, counted off the RMS track rather than inferred from a spectrum.
16218               	; 	' (colecosounds variant 1A; assets/sfx/sfxref-coleco.md has the working.)
16219               	; 	'
16220               	; 	' 104 px/s over 14 px is 7.43 a second. 13 px would give 8.00, and 7.7 sits
16221               	; 	' almost exactly between them -- so this is the nearer of the two, and it is
16222               	; 	' also the one that does not walk back into the 8.0 that was rejected by ear.
16223               	; 	'
16224               	; 	' WHY THE GAME KEEPS A DISTANCE AND THE BENCH KEEPS A CADENCE. The bench
16225               	; 	' plays a fixed eight frames between steps because it has no walking to tie
16226               	; 	' them to; the game accumulates PIXELS TRAVELLED, so the feet keep time with
16227               	; 	' the legs when he is slowed or stopped. Matching "7.4 a second" therefore
16228               	; 	' means matching it AT HIS WALKING SPEED, and assumes the ColecoVision's
16229               	; 	' crook walks at ours -- which the recording cannot confirm.
16230               	; 	'
16231               	; 	' The dial is this one constant and the subtraction below, which must stay
16232               	; 	' threshold + 1 or the carry is wrong.
16233               	; 	'
16234               	; 	' SOT = 2 IS THE SHORTEST TICK THERE IS, and 1 is SILENCE. The decay block
16235               	; 	' below runs LATER IN THE SAME sfx_tick, so a count of 1 is decremented to
16236               	; 	' zero on the pass that set it and the note-off fires before the sound has
16237               	; 	' lasted any time at all. 2 survives to the next pass, which is one pass of
16238               	; 	' sound -- about 42 ms against the bench's 33, as close as a per-pass timer
16239               	; 	' gets, and the reason the bench and the game cannot sound identical.
16240               	; 	'
16241               	; 	' Register 4 is white noise at the fastest rate.
16242               	; 	'
16243               	; 	' VOLUME 9, WHICH IS UNDER EVERYTHING ELSE ON PURPOSE. The hit, the prize
16244               	; 	' and the jump are 12 and 13, and they happen ONCE; footsteps play for the
16245               	; 	' whole round. At 13 they were level with the events they are supposed to
16246               	; 	' sit beneath, so the effects that carry information had nothing to stand
16247               	; 	' out from. The tone version was 7 for the same reason -- noise does read
16248               	; 	' quieter than a tone at the same number, which is why this is 9 and not
16249               	; 	' back to 7.

16448               	;
16449               	; 	' EVERYTHING BELOW THIS LINE IS ASSEMBLED INTO BANK 1, so the INCLUDE order
16450               	; 	' is load-bearing and nothing but data may follow it.
16451               	; 	'
16452               	; 	' THE FONT IS NOW IN THE BANK TOO, and it used to be deliberately outside:
16453               	; 	' keeping one readable thing in bank 0 means a bank-selection mistake shows
16454               	; 	' as "text survives, art does not" rather than a uniformly blank screen,
16455               	; 	' which is a genuinely useful thing to have when a bank goes wrong.
16456               	; 	'
16457               	; 	' THE FONT HAS A BANK OF ITS OWN, and the reason is not its size.
16458               	; 	'
16459               	; 	' Bank 1 was FULL -- six spare bytes of 8,192 -- which shut the door on
16460               	; 	' moving anything else out of the fixed area, and the fixed area is the
16461               	; 	' only budget that cannot be grown (linkticart writes exactly three
16462               	; 	' loader pages and discards the rest; they are the 32K expansion's RAM at
16463               	; 	' >A000, not cart ROM). A second bank costs a bigger cart -- five pages
16464               	; 	' round up to eight, so 32 KB becomes 64 KB -- and buys back the ability
16465               	; 	' to keep evacuating data out of code.
16466               	; 	'
16467               	; 	' THE FONT IS THE RIGHT TENANT because it is read ONCE. Two DEFINEs copy
16468               	; 	' it into VRAM at setup and nothing looks at it again, so it is the only
16469               	; 	' block here that can sit on a page which is not permanently mapped. See
16470               	; 	' setup_font: bank 2 is selected for those two statements and bank 1 for
16471               	; 	' the whole of the rest of the program.
16472               	; 	'
16473               	; 	' EVERYTHING ELSE STAYS IN BANK 1, because everything else is read during
16474               	; 	' play -- art on a screen crossing, templates on a band blit, the lookup
16475               	; 	' tables every pass. One permanently-mapped bank for all of it means
16476               	; 	' there is no switch to miss.
16477               	; 	#if TI994A
16478               	; 	BANK 2
16479      0A7E     BANK_0_FREE:	EQU >fffe-$

16617               	;
16618               	; 	' THE COLOUR TABLE, 472 bytes of the same value ($B4 = black ink on dark blue).
16619               	; 	'
16620               	; 	' Loaded with DEFINE COLOR 32,59,font_col, which is ONE synchronous call that
16621               	; 	' writes all three screen thirds (define_color always does the LDIRVM3 triple
16622               	; 	' copy). It replaced a VPOKE loop that wrote this one value 1,416 times paced by
16623               	; 	' 24 WAITs -- the largest scripted delay in the boot, and the reason the title
16624               	; 	' screen used to fill in visibly rather than appearing at once.
16625               	; 	'
16626               	; 	' EIGHT BYTES PER CHARACTER, not one. Supply fewer and DEFINE COLOR reads
16627               	; 	' whatever follows in ROM as colour data, with no error at build or run time.
16628               	;
16629               	; font_col:
16630               cvb_FONT_COL

17064               	; 	INCLUDE "titledl.bas"
17065               	; 	' ==================================================
17066               	; 	' THE TITLE SCREEN, AS A DISPLAY LIST
17067               	; 	' Generated by assets/gentitle.py -- do not edit here.
17068               	; 	'
17069               	; 	' row, col, length, then `length` bytes; 255 ends.
17070               	; 	' Walked by title_draw only.
17071               	; 	'
17072               	; 	' LIVES IN BANK 2, with the fonts, because it is read ONCE
17073               	; 	' -- at boot and on a return to the title. title_draw
17074               	; 	' selects bank 2 around its walk and restores bank 1.
17075               	; 	' The message boxes in title.bas are the same format and
17076               	; 	' CANNOT come with it: they are read when a round ends.
17077               	; 	' ==================================================

18537               	; 	INCLUDE "store.bas"
18538               	; 	' Keystone Kapers store -- GENERATED by assets/genstore.py. Do not edit.
18539               	; 	'
18540               	; 	' EIGHT band templates of 5 rows x 32 cols (160 bytes each) plus a 32-byte
18541               	; 	' index over (level, screen). The whole 8-screen, 4-level building is about
18542               	; 	' 1.3 KB instead of the 5,120 bytes it would cost to store literally.
18543               	; 	'
18544               	; 	' All eight templates are ONE contiguous block under ONE label, so a band
18545               	; 	' blit is
18546               	; 	'     SCREEN stor_tpl, tpl*160, toprow*32, 32, 5, 32
18547               	; 	' with no label ladder -- SCREEN needs a literal label and a label cannot be
18548               	; 	' chosen by a variable, which is why RallyX needed a 4-way IF over its maze
18549               	; 	' tables. One block sidesteps it.
18550               	; 	'
18551               	; 	' 160 is EVEN, so this cannot leave the location counter odd and misalign
18552               	; 	' the word tables defined after it.
18553               	; 	'
18554               	; 	' template ids:
18555               	; 	'   0 T_AISLE_A
18556               	; 	'   1 T_AISLE_B
18557               	; 	'   2 T_ESC_W
18558               	; 	'   3 T_ESC_E
18559               	; 	'   4 T_ELEV
18560               	; 	'   5 T_ROOF0
18561               	; 	'   6 T_ROOF1
18562               	; 	'   7 T_ROOF2
18563               	; 	'   8 T_ROOF3
18564               	; 	'   9 T_ROOF4
18565               	; 	'   10 T_ROOF5
18566               	; 	'   11 T_ROOF6
18567               	; 	'   12 T_ROOF7
18568               	; 	'   13 T_END_W
18569               	; 	'   14 T_END_E
18570               	;
18571               	; stor_tpl:	' 15 templates x 160 bytes
18572               cvb_STOR_TPL

19187               	;
19188               	; 	' THE SKYLINE'S LAST BAND WITHOUT ITS YELLOW, high nibble ink, low nibble
19189               	; 	' paper, one byte a scan line -- the same shape genart emits into
19190               	; 	' store_col. SKY2 is white-on-9 throughout instead of turning to paper 10
19191               	; 	' at row 4; BLDGL holds its blue one row longer and then meets its own
19192               	; 	' grey wall. Both are the generated bytes with 10 replaced by 9 and
19193               	; 	' nothing else changed. See setup_rest.
19194               	; #if NES
19195               	; nes_sky2c:
19196               	; 	DATA BYTE $F9,$F9,$F9,$F9,$F9,$F9,$F9,$F9
19197               	; nes_bldlc:
19198               	; 	DATA BYTE $B9,$B9,$B9,$B9,$B9,$BE,$BE,$BE
19199               	; #endif
19200               	;
19201               	; 	' THE IN-GAME FONT'S COLOUR, one byte a scan line and eight a character for
19202               	; 	' all 59 of them. $B4 is light yellow on dark blue -- ink index 3, paper index 1 --
19203               	; 	' and which colours those are is then the attribute table's business, per
19204               	; 	' region: dark blue behind the HUD, the store's green behind a message box.
19205               	; 	'
19206               	; 	' 472 bytes of one repeated value. That reads like waste and is the cheap
19207               	; 	' option: ROM is three budgets here and this is not the scarce one, while
19208               	; 	' the alternative is a second font (impossible -- only eleven free codes)
19209               	; 	' or a new uploader parameter (no RAM -- two bytes left).

19211               	; nes_fcol:
